source_refs.note: Exercise 12.2, Question 5 (i)-(ii): find m and n for continuity at x = 3 (book p.234); part (ii) has no n. Answer key PDF 310 prints m = 4 for (ii); correct m = 3.

blocks.prompt: 5 (i) Find the values \(m\) and \(n\), so that given function \(f\) is continuous at \(x = 3\): \[f(x) = \begin{cases} mx, & x < 3 \\ n, & x = 3 \\ -2x + 9, & x > 3 \end{cases}\]
blocks.explanation:
A "find the constants" continuity question.
Continuity at \(x = 3\) needs LHL = RHL = \(f(3)\): two unknowns, two equations.
Plan: find the RHL (a number), then make the LHL and \(f(3)\) equal to it.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = mx\) for \(x < 3\), \(f(3) = n\), \(f(x) = -2x + 9\) for \(x > 3\).
To find: \(m\) and \(n\) so that \(f\) is continuous at \(x = 3\).
Method: Continuity at 3 means \(\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = f(3)\).

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^-} mx = 3m\]
Why: Left of 3 the first piece \(mx\) is used.

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} (-2x + 9)\]
\[= -6 + 9 = 3\]
Why: Right of 3 the third piece is used.

Value at the point
\[f(3) = n\]
Why: The middle line gives the value at \(x = 3\).

Make the three equal
\[3m = 3 \Rightarrow m = 1\]
\[n = 3\]
Why: The LHL must equal the RHL (3), and \(f(3)\) must equal the limit (3).

Check
\[m = 1:\ \lim_{x \to 3^-} x = 3\]
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = f(3) = 3\]
Why: All three conditions of continuity hold with \(m = 1,\ n = 3\).

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) Find the values \(m\) and \(n\), so that given function \(f\) is continuous at \(x = 3\): \[f(x) = \begin{cases} mx, & x < 3 \\ x^2, & x \ge 3 \end{cases}\]
blocks.explanation:
A "find the constant" continuity question; this part has only one unknown, \(m\) (there is no \(n\) in it).
Continuity at \(x = 3\) needs LHL = RHL = \(f(3)\).
Plan: find \(f(3)\) and the RHL from \(x^2\), then make the LHL \(3m\) equal to them.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = mx\) for \(x < 3\), \(f(x) = x^2\) for \(x \ge 3\).
To find: \(m\) so that \(f\) is continuous at \(x = 3\).
Method: Continuity at 3 means \(\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = f(3)\).

Value at the point
\[f(3) = 3^2 = 9\]
Why: \(x \ge 3\) includes 3, so the piece \(x^2\) gives \(f(3)\).

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} x^2 = 9\]
Why: Right of 3 the same piece \(x^2\) is used.

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^-} mx = 3m\]
Why: Left of 3 the piece \(mx\) is used.

Make them equal and solve
\[3m = 9\]
\[m = \frac{9}{3} = 3\]
Why: The LHL must equal the RHL and \(f(3)\), which are both 9.

Check
\[m = 3:\ \lim_{x \to 3^-} 3x = 9\]
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = f(3) = 9\]
Why: All three conditions hold with \(m = 3\). (With \(m = 4\) the LHL would be 12, not 9.)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints "(ii) \(m = 4\)". This is wrong: continuity at \(x = 3\) needs \(3m = 3^2 = 9\), so \(m = 3\). With \(m = 4\) the left hand limit is 12, which does not equal \(f(3) = 9\).
